newsitem.title: JAPAN: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Mar 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Mar 24.

text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Japanese press on Monday, as reported by Kyodo news agency:
-- U.S. Vice President Albert Gore says it is difficult to reduce the number of U.S. marines based in Japan.
-- The Japanese government to allow the conversion of real-estate mortgages into bonds.
-- Gore says the United States to keep 100,000 troops in East Asia.
-- Three ex-Green Cross Corp presidents likely to admit guilt in HIV-contaminated drugs trial today.
-- Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) of Peru wants fewer than 100 jailed comrades released.
-- Japan and the United States to cooperate on environmental protection.
-- Fifty-eight percent of Diet members favor revision of special military bases law in Yomiuri poll.
-- Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori hints of final phase of negotiations with hostage-takers.
